To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed and implemented a high-level approach, called the Java Skeleton Programming System, that allows the application programmer to write a parallel and distributed application in terms of high-level components called skeletons, and that this system can be used to implement the Barnes-Hut N-body algorithm in a way that hides many complex details of parallel and distributed programming, and achieves good performance.

we can build a grid application programming environment based on high-level programming abstractions and that we can use this environment to program and run non-trivial, dynamically changing grid applications.

we propose and implement a high-level approach for programming and load-balanced execution of grid applications based on a generic component model with integrated load-balancing, that we use this approach to implement a non-trivial application – Barnes-Hut algorithm, and that we achieve good performance on an experiment grid testbed.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and evaluation of a programming model that allows the programmer to express the parallelism of a problem in terms of a set of computational tasks, and to specify how those tasks should be executed on the underlying distributed system, while hiding many of the complex details of the underlying system.
the development of a programming system for the Grid that is easy to use for application programmers.
developing high-level programming systems for grid computing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of skeletons and the proposed programming approach is very promising, and the results are encouraging.
the proposed approach has a potential to be a useful tool for grid programming.
the proposed approach to grid programming is feasible and promising.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that a high-level grid programming system with integrated load-balancing can work well on real grid testbeds.
Towards High-Level Grid Computing with Integrated Load-Balancing.
we have developed a high-level grid programming system, with skeletons, and have applied this system to the Barnes-Hut case.
we have shown that the use of skeletons and the use of dynamic load-balancing are complementary, and that the combination of the two is a very powerful and effective approach for grid programming.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high-level grid application programming is possible and that the proposed approach is a promising direction for further research.
high-level grid programming is feasible, and that the use of generic components with integrated load-balancing is a promising approach to grid programming.
the use of high-level skeletons can simplify the development of complex, dynamic grid applications, while providing performance close to that of a hand-coded, low-level implementation.
